articles.title: A Multimodal Intervention Model Integrating Cognitive Behavioral Education and Health Care Collaboration for Flatfoot Prevention in Children: A Multicentre Cohort Study and Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Ouyang Y, Zhao Y, Ma W, Li J, Gu Q
articles.study_type: Multicentre randomised controlled trial with cohort screening
articles.population: Children aged 7 to 12 years; 540 with confirmed flexible flatfoot randomised to three groups
articles.outcomes: Arch index change at 12 months (primary); gait symmetry, pain relief, compliance rate, and functional outcomes (secondary)
articles.take_home: A combined approach using dynamic foot analysis, artificial intelligence assessment, education about foot health, and custom arch supports improved flatfoot in children better than traditional insoles alone, with better pain relief and higher completion rates. The study found flatfoot affects about 28 per cent of Asian children aged 7 to 12, with highest rates at age 7.

articles.title: Arthrogram findings of displaced annular ligament in paediatric Monteggia injuries: Introducing the "Rose Thorn" sign of the elbow.
articles.authors: Khan AM, Power FR, Loh BW, Donnan L, Wang KK
articles.population: Skeletally immature patients with acute Monteggia injuries
articles.outcomes: Presence of Rose Thorn sign on arthrogram correlated with annular ligament displacement and persistent radial head instability
articles.take_home: A new X-ray finding called the Rose Thorn sign can help surgeons identify when the annular ligament is trapped during treatment of Monteggia fractures in children, allowing them to know when additional surgery is needed to stabilise the radial head.

articles.title: Risk factors for growth disturbance in children with surgically treated distal femoral epiphyseal fractures.
articles.authors: Xue C, Huang D, Liang X, Lin W, Yao H, Chen Y, et al.
articles.population: Children with surgically treated distal femoral epiphyseal fractures
articles.outcomes: Post-traumatic growth disturbance, knee range of motion, KOOS-Child scores, angular deformities, leg length discrepancy
articles.take_home: Growth problems occurred in about one third of children after surgery for this type of fracture. Surgery performed more than 7.5 days after injury and greater fracture displacement increased the risk of these growth problems, which also led to reduced knee movement and lower function scores.

articles.title: Need for removal of flexible intramedullary nails used to treat femoral shaft fractures in children: an observational study of 55 children with a minimum of 5-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Nietosvaara NR, Kosola J, Nietosvaara Y, Puhakka J, Helenius I, Laaksonen T
articles.population: Children aged 3-14 years with femoral shaft fractures treated with flexible intramedullary nails
articles.outcomes: Frequency and timing of nail removal, comparison of removal rates between correctly placed nails and nails that were too long
articles.take_home: About two-thirds of children needed their flexible intramedullary nails removed, mostly because of pain, within a median of 2.4 years after surgery. Nails that extended too far down the thigh bone were much more likely to need removing than correctly placed nails.

articles.title: Reliability of Ultrasound-Based Metrics for Patellofemoral Instability: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Jain D, Kim A, Kim C, Dykes C, Harwood K, Greenberg E, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of ultrasound-based metrics for patellofemoral instability
articles.sample_size: 3263 knees in 1997 patients across 33 included studies
articles.outcomes: Reliability of ultrasound measurements of trochlear morphology, patellar height, axial alignment, dynamic patellar tracking, and soft tissue or osteochondral pathology; accuracy for detecting abnormalities
articles.take_home: Ultrasound is reliable for measuring bone shape of the knee joint (particularly the groove at the bottom of the thigh bone and kneecap height) and accurately detects soft tissue and cartilage damage, suggesting it could be a useful alternative to MRI and CT scans. However, more work is needed to standardise how the scans are done before it becomes routine in everyday practice.

articles.title: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21/Matrix-M against malaria in The Gambia and Burkina Faso: an open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.
articles.authors: Dabira ED, Natama HM, Erhart A, Bihoun B, Keita ML, Derra K, et al.
articles.population: Residents aged 5 months and older in malaria-endemic villages in The Gambia and Burkina Faso
articles.sample_size: 54 villages (30 in The Gambia, 24 in Burkina Faso); 2565 vaccinated in The Gambia, 4072 in Burkina Faso
articles.outcomes: Malaria prevalence at peak transmission measured by presence of Plasmodium falciparum infection; adverse events
articles.take_home: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21 malaria vaccine reduced malaria infection by 70% in The Gambia and 25% in Burkina Faso, with the vaccine being safe and well tolerated. This suggests the vaccine could help control malaria in areas with seasonal transmission patterns.

articles.title: Opioid Prescribing Calibration, Consumption, and Disposal After Posterior Spinal Fusion for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: A 7-year Institutional Stewardship Analysis.
articles.authors: Gamadia M, Stuedemann A, Edmundson L, Benvenuti M, Schwend RM, Anderson JT, et al.
articles.population: Adolescents aged 10 to 20 years undergoing posterior spinal fusion for idiopathic scoliosis
articles.sample_size: 321 patients (275 for prescribing analysis; 79 to 115 for consumption and disposal surveys)
articles.outcomes: Opioid tablet prescription volume, caregiver-reported consumption, unused medication proportion, household disposal rates, and patient satisfaction with pain management
articles.take_home: Opioid prescriptions after spinal fusion surgery for teenage scoliosis fell by two-thirds over seven years, with most patients using fewer tablets than prescribed, yet only a small proportion disposed of leftover medications safely. Patient satisfaction and requests for additional pain relief remained unchanged despite lower prescriptions.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Cast Slippage After the Ponseti Method for Congenital Idiopathic Clubfoot: A Retrospective Analysis.
articles.authors: Jiang J, Li S, Li L, Chen Q, Liu M, Wang D
articles.population: Infants with congenital idiopathic clubfoot treated with the Ponseti method
articles.outcomes: Cast slippage occurred in 19 patients (11.7%), with equinus deviation and increased thigh-to-calf girth ratio identified as independent risk factors
articles.take_home: During Ponseti casting for clubfoot, cast slippage happens in about 1 in 9 infants. The study found that babies with certain foot shape characteristics (equinus deviation) and those with a larger thigh compared to calf size are at higher risk of their cast slipping off, which doctors can watch for more carefully.

articles.title: 3D Ultrasound Measurements Better Predict Residual Acetabular Dysplasia Following Successful Pavlik Treatment of DDH Compared With 2D Metrics Alone.
articles.authors: Blanchard S, Hall CE, Ullmann OC, McArthur A, Sarkar S, Jaremko J, et al.
articles.population: Infants with developmental dysplasia of the hip treated with Pavlik harness
articles.outcomes: Residual acetabular dysplasia on follow-up pelvic radiographs at 6 months after treatment; predictive accuracy of 2D versus 3D ultrasound measurements
articles.take_home: Even when hips appeared normal on standard ultrasound scans during Pavlik harness treatment, one in six infants still showed persistent hip dysplasia on X-rays 6 months later. Three-dimensional ultrasound measurements, particularly a new measurement called the acetabular contact angle, were better at predicting which hips would have this residual dysplasia compared to the traditional two-dimensional measurements alone.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes of 4 Treatment Strategies for Late-Onset Legg-Calve-Perthes Disease.
articles.authors: Abril JC, Garcia-Fernandez J, Munoz-Vicente A, Rey-Canas R
articles.population: Children with late-onset Legg-Calve-Perthes disease (onset after 8 years of age) followed until skeletal maturity
articles.sample_size: 95 hips: 26 conservative treatment, 26 femoral varus osteotomy, 15 shelf acetabular osteotomy, 28 arthrodiastasis with epiphysiodesis
articles.outcomes: Radiographic outcomes (Stulberg grade, sphericity deviation score, residual osteochondritis), leg-length discrepancy, modified Harris Hip Score
articles.take_home: Arthrodiastasis with epiphysiodesis produced better long-term hip shape and function compared with conservative treatment, femoral varus osteotomy, or shelf acetabular osteotomy in children with late-onset Legg-Calve-Perthes disease. Patients treated with arthrodiastasis had less leg-length difference, less cartilage damage, and higher hip function scores.

articles.title: Immediate versus delayed MRI following medial open reduction for developmental dysplasia of the hip: Re-intervention rates and resource utilisation.
articles.authors: Mil M, Hyde N, Moorhead R, Loh B, Donnan L
articles.population: Children under 10 years undergoing medial open reduction for developmental dysplasia of the hip
articles.outcomes: Re-intervention rates, theatre duration, length of hospital stay, and estimated costs
articles.take_home: Doing an MRI scan the day after surgery rather than immediately during surgery did not significantly increase the need for further operations, though it may be slightly less safe. Waiting until the next day avoided longer time in theatre and reduced hospital stay, suggesting it could be a more cost-effective approach for selected cases.

articles.title: Pediatric and adolescent pathological fractures: Etiological spectrum, biomechanical instability, and individualized treatment strategies - a current concepts review.
articles.authors: Krieg AH, van de Sande M, Balaco I, Salom-Taverner M, Helenius I, Wirth T, et al.
articles.population: Children and adolescents with pathological fractures
articles.outcomes: Etiological spectrum, biomechanical instability, and individualized treatment strategies for pathological fractures
articles.take_home: Pathological fractures in children are rare but need careful evaluation to identify the underlying cause before treating the fracture itself. Treatment should aim not only to heal the fracture but also to prevent future breaks and protect the child's growth potential.

articles.title: The Banff Patellofemoral Instability Instrument 2.0 : structural validity and responsiveness as a patient-centred tool for assessing recovery after medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Sze IN, Kerslake S, Hiemstra LA
articles.study_type: Validation study of a patient-reported outcome measure
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 731 patients (828 knees); 526 completed full assessment battery
articles.outcomes: Structural validity, internal consistency, construct validity, floor and ceiling effects, and responsiveness of the Banff Patellofemoral Instability Instrument 2.0 across five domains measured preoperatively and at 6, 12, and 24 months after surgery
articles.take_home: The Banff Patellofemoral Instability Instrument 2.0 is a reliable and valid questionnaire for measuring patient recovery after kneecap ligament reconstruction surgery, with most improvement happening in the first six months and continued gains up to two years in work, lifestyle and emotional wellbeing.

articles.title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age.
articles.authors: Jastreboff AM, Harder-Lauridsen NM, Van Name M, Korner A, Kelly AS, Weghuber D, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 6 to under 12 years with obesity
articles.outcomes: BMI reduction, BMI category reduction, return to non-obese BMI range
articles.take_home: Children taking semaglutide for 68 weeks had their BMI reduce by 13.5% compared to a 2.7% increase with placebo. More than three-quarters of children on semaglutide moved down a BMI category, and over a third reached a healthy BMI range, compared to very few in the placebo group.

articles.title: Tibiofibular Relationships in Children With Achondroplasia: A Comparative Radiographic Study.
articles.authors: Rovira Marti MP, Garcia Fontecha CG, Torner Rubies F
articles.population: Children younger than 21 years with achondroplasia compared with controls without conditions affecting lower-limb alignment
articles.sample_size: 121 children (63 with achondroplasia, 58 controls) contributing 239 radiographic examinations
articles.outcomes: Tibiofibular relationships measured by plateau-fibula distance, fibular extension measurement, fibula-to-tibia length ratio, and associations with lower-limb alignment parameters including mechanical axis deviation, proximal tibial angle, and distal tibial angle
articles.take_home: Children with achondroplasia have relative overgrowth of the fibula compared with the tibia, which is associated with increased bowlegging and altered alignment of the leg. The findings may help guide surgical planning for leg lengthening procedures in these children.

articles.title: Comparison of responses from large language models using artificial intelligence for parent-focused inquiries on clubfoot treatment and Ponseti management.
articles.authors: Vescio A, Testa G, Sapienza M, Caldaci A, Familiari F, Donati F, et al.
articles.population: Responses to parent questions about clubfoot treatment, evaluated by paediatric orthopaedic surgeons
articles.sample_size: 45 responses (15 questions submitted to 3 AI language models)
articles.outcomes: Accuracy, completeness, and readability of AI-generated responses about Ponseti method for clubfoot treatment
articles.take_home: Google Gemini gave the most accurate and complete answers about clubfoot treatment with the Ponseti method, but its responses were longer and more complex. ChatGPT-4.0 was easier to read but gave less detailed answers.
